🔈 The Work Behind a Crypto Exchange

Ever wondered what actually happens after you place a trade on a centralized crypto exchange?

The process involves much more than matching buyers and sellers.

Trading systems process orders, internal records track balances, financial operations investigate discrepancie and risk and support teams help handle unexpected issues.

Our latest article explains how these processes work together and the different professional responsibilities involved.

It's a useful look at why crypto exchanges need people working across engineering, finance, operations, security, compliance and customer support.

item.title: 💗 📄 Your resume might have the right experience, but is it showing the right inf
item.description:
💗 📄 Your resume might have the right experience, but is it showing the right information?

One mistake job seekers make is using the exact same resume for every position, even when the requirements are different.

You don't need to rewrite your entire resume for each application. A few targeted changes can make your relevant experience easier to identify.

Here's what to focus on:

1. Review the job description first.
Identify the main responsibilities, required skills and tools mentioned in the listing.

2. Adjust your professional summary.
Highlight the experience most relevant to the position instead of using the same generic introduction everywhere.

3. Reorder your bullet points.
If a position emphasizes customer support, for example, make your relevant support experience more visible rather than burying it beneath unrelated responsibilities.

4. Use specific language.
Replace vague descriptions like “helped with various tasks” with clear explanations of what you actually did.

5. Include relevant keywords naturally.
Use accurate terminology from the job description where it reflects your real experience. Don't add skills you don't have just to match the listing.

The goal isn't to make yourself look like a different candidate for every application.

It's to make it easier for hiring teams to recognize why your existing experience is relevant.

Before sending your next application, spend a few minutes reviewing your resume from the employer's perspective.

item.title: 💗 Recruiter screening vs. hiring manager interview: What's the difference? You m
item.description:
💗 Recruiter screening vs. hiring manager interview: What's the difference?

You might be asked about your experience in both interviews, but each conversation usually has a different purpose.

1. Recruiter screening - Are you a potential match?
This is often the first conversation in the hiring process.
The recruiter typically wants to understand your background, why you're interested in the position, your salary expectations, availability and whether the employment arrangements work for both sides.

They're usually checking whether it makes sense to move forward.

2. Hiring manager interview - How would you actually do the job?

This conversation tends to go deeper into your skills, experience and approach to work.

Instead of simply confirming that you've done something before, the hiring manager might ask how you handled a particular challenge, why you made certain decisions and what results you achieved.

🔜 So, how should you prepare?

For recruiter screenings, practice explaining your background clearly and be ready to discuss practical expectations.

For hiring manager interviews, prepare specific examples that demonstrate how you work, solve problems and make decisions.

Not every company follows this exact structure, but understanding what each conversation is meant to evaluate can help you prepare more effectively.

item.title: 💗 The company reposted the job you applied for. Does that mean you were rejected
item.description:
💗 The company reposted the job you applied for. Does that mean you were rejected?

Not necessarily. And it doesn't automatically mean you should apply again.

There are several reasons a company might repost a vacancy, even while applications are being reviewed.

1. They haven't found the right candidate yet
The company may still be interviewing people but wants to attract additional applicants before making a decision.

2. The listing was refreshed automatically
Some job platforms allow employers to renew vacancies to keep them visible. The hiring process might not have changed at all.

3. The job requirements have changed
After reviewing applications, the hiring team may realize it needs a different level of experience, additional skills or someone in a specific location.

4. They're hiring more than one person
Two openings can have the same title but represent separate positions within the team.

🔜 So, should you apply again?

It depends on where you are in the process.

• Applied recently? Check your application status before submitting another one.

• The job description changed? Compare the requirements. If the updated position is a better match, consider following up or submitting a new application.

• Already interviewed? A short message to the recruiter asking about your status is more useful than sending another identical application.

• Received a rejection? Don't assume a repost means the decision has changed. Reapply if there's a meaningful reason your candidacy should be reconsidered.

The key takeaway: A reposted job doesn't confirm rejection, but it doesn't guarantee you're still being considered either.

Before taking action, check what's actually changed.
